CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  2175 Cherry Avenue • Signal Hill, California 90755-3799

  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  WELCOMES YOU TO A REGULAR
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  April 25, 2023

Meetings begin at 6:30 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in
closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with
the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment
on closed session matters at 6:30 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no
business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm.
There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting. Any person
wishing to comment shall be allotted three minutes per distinct item. Any meeting may be
adjourned to a time and place stated in the order of adjournment.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting on the City’s website and outside of City
Hall. The agenda and related reports are also available for review online at
www.cityofsignalhill.org.

To view or listen to the meeting live at 7:00 p.m.:

  • City of Signal Hill website at www.cityofsignalhill.org, select the City Council
  Meetings Link from the home page.
  • Charter Spectrum Channel 3 or Frontier FiOS Channel 38.
  • Call (408) 638-0968 (audio only) and enter meeting ID: 881-4793-6648, press #
  when prompted to provide participant ID, and enter passcode: 374778. If you would like
  to make a public comment, please notify the meeting host by pressing *9 on the
  telephone keypad.
To view and participate (closed session at 6:30 p.m. and regular meeting at 7:00 p.m.):

  • In-person Participation: Council Chambers of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal
  Hill, California.
  • Remote Participation: Visit https://zoom.us/j/88147936648 on your desktop
  computer or laptop and enter passcode: 374778; or
  • Visit www.zoom.us on your desktop computer or laptop, click on “Join a Meeting”,
  and enter meeting ID: 881-4793-6648 and passcode: 374778 when prompted; or
  • Download the app from the app store if you are using a smart phone and enter
  meeting ID: 881-4793-6648 and passcode: 374778 when prompted.

  Page 1 of 9
 City Council  Regular  April 25, 2023

  • Please note that you will be placed in a “listen only” mode and your video feed will
  not be shared with the Council or public. If you would like to make a public comment,
  please notify the meeting host by raising your virtual hand (see hand icon at bottom of
  screen) and you will be invited to speak when the City Council is taking public
  comments. Please do not simultaneously use a microphone through Zoom and a
  cellphone/telephone. That combination results in audio problems for all participants.
  • To make a general public comment or comment on a specific agenda item, you may
  also submit your comment, limited to 250 words or less, to the City Clerk at
  cityclerk@cityofsignalhill.org not later than 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, April 25, 2023.
  Written comments will be provided electronically to City Council and attached to the
  meeting minutes. Written comments will not be read into the record.
  • Please note that remote participation is offered as a public service and the City is
  not responsible for meeting disruptions or technical difficulties; however, if you are
  disconnected, please repeat the steps above. Submission of written comments or
  in-person participation will ensure that your comments are received.
City Council Members are compensated $722.18 per month. City Clerk and City Treasurer are
compensated $438.22 per month.

(12)  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

  a.  INTERVIEWS AND APPOINTMENTS TO THE CIVIL SERVICE, PARKS AND
  RECREATION, AND PLANNING COMMISSIONS

  Summary:

  The City ran an open recruitment seeking residents interested in serving on the
  Civil Service, Parks and Recreation, and Planning Commissions. The City
  Council will conduct interviews of all qualifying candidates who applied for a
  Commission appointment. At the conclusion of the interviews, City Council will
  make appointments to fill the vacant seats on each of the Commissions.
  Recommendations:

  Conduct interviews and make the following appointments:

  1. Civil Service Commission: Appoint two individuals to fill two expiring seats
  (May 31, 2023). Terms for the new Commissioners will run from June 1,
  2023 - May 31, 2027.

  2. Parks and Recreation Commission: Appoint two individuals to fill two expiring
  seats (May 31, 2023). Terms for the new Commissioners will run from June
  1, 2023 - May 31, 2027.

  3. Planning Commission: Appoint two individuals to fill two expiring seats (May
  31, 2023). Terms for the new Commissioners will run from June 1, 2023 -
  May 31, 2027.

  Page 3 of 9
 City Council  Regular  April 25, 2023

  b.  PROCESS TO FILL A CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION VACANCY

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider a process to fill one vacancy on the Civil Service
  Commission for an unexpired term through May 31, 2025.
  Recommendations:

  1. Approve the proposed recruitment schedule and select a date to conduct
  commissioner candidate interviews and appointment. The suggested date is
  the regular City Council meeting of May 23, 2023. If the number of
  commission applicants is greater than ten, City Council may wish to call a
  special meeting for June 1 or June 6, 2023.

  2. As an alternative, provide staff direction to utilize the recent list of Civil
  Service applicants from the recruitment that concluded April 14, 2023 and
  invite applicants to interview at the May 23, 2023 City Council meeting.
  c.  OUTDOOR PUBLIC ART PROJECT BUDGET ADJUSTMENT

  Summary:

  The City has a history of incorporating art into parks and public facilities. With
  the opening of the Signal Hill Library, the City Council desired to enhance the
  facility by encouraging creative expression. To effectuate this purpose, the City
  issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) for an outdoor public art project and
  formed a subcommittee to review responses. The City issued the RFP twice
  and did not successfully identify a qualified artist that could fulfill the project
  requirements for $50,000. Staff contacted local artists to obtain additional
  feedback regarding the criteria in the RFP and discuss whether the proposed
  compensation was sufficient to fulfill the City’s vision. After consulting with
  various artists, staff recommends reissuing the RFP and increasing the project
  budget amount. Staff is seeking the City Council’s concurrence to reissue the
  RFP and increase the project budget by $30,000. The additional funding would
  come from the unallocated General Fund for a total project budget of $80,000.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize staff to reissue the RFP for the Outdoor Public Arts Project at the
  Signal Hill Library.

  2. Approve the proposed increase of $30,000 for a total project allocation of
  $80,000. The increased budget would be reflected in the FY 2023-24 Year 2
  proposed budget.
  d.  PROFESSIONAL CONSULTANT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ARDURRA
  GROUP, INC. (AGI) FOR ENGINEERING DESIGN OF THE GUNDRY
  RESERVOIR ROOF REPLACEMENT AND INTERIOR COATING PROJECT
  (PROJECT NO. 95.23001)

  Page 4 of 9
 City Council  Regular  April 25, 2023

  Summary:

  On February 9, 2023, staff issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) for Gundry
  Reservoir Roof Replacement and Interior Coating Design Services. The City
  Council will consider entering into a Professional Consultant Services
  Agreement with AGI for engineering design of the Gundry Reservoir Roof
  Replacement and Interior Coating Project (Project No. 95.23001).
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a Professional Consultant Services
  Agreement with AGI for engineering design of the Gundry Reservoir Roof
  Replacement and Interior Coating Project (Project No. 95.23001), in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. The term of the agreement will terminate on
  June 30, 2024, with a not-to-exceed contract amount of $299,313.

  2. Authorize contingencies of $29,931.30 and up to a 180-day term extension
  pursuant to the City’s Purchasing and Contracting Guidelines, to be utilized if
  approved by the Public Works Director.
  e.  REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) FOR THE PREPARATION OF A CIVIC
  CENTER MASTER PLAN

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider authorizing the City Manager to solicit an RFP for
  preparation of a master plan for the City’s Civic Center. The Master Plan will
  guide future improvements and development of the Civic Center based on the
  prioritization of community needs and desires. The document will include
  preliminary site designs, conceptual drawings, as well as schedules and
  preliminary cost estimates for construction. The Master Plan will also explore
  siting options for a new amphitheater, either as a standalone structure or in
  conjunction with a project to build a new Community Center. The services are
  expected to be completed within six (6) months from the City’s issuance of a
  Notice to Proceed.
  Recommendation:

  Direct the City Manager to issue an RFP for the preparation of a master plan for
  the City’s Civic Center and solicit proposals from qualified consultants.
CALL THE HOUSING AUTHORITY TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

  CHAIR HANSEN
  VICE CHAIR WOODS
  MEMBER COPELAND
  MEMBER JONES
  MEMBER WILSON

  Page 5 of 9
 City Council  Regular  April 25, 2023

  f.  NOTICE OF FUNDING AVAILABILITY (NOFA) FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF
  THE ORANGE BLUFF AND WALNUT BLUFF WORKFORCE HOUSING SITES
  AND SOLICIT PROPOSALS FROM QUALIFIED AFFORDABLE HOUSING
  DEVELOPERS

  Summary:

  Last year, the State Department of Housing and Community Development
  certified the City’s Housing Element, which included two sites specifically entitled
  for the development of workforce housing. Known as Orange Bluff and Walnut
  Bluff, the properties are comprised of 8.6 and 2.0 acres of undeveloped property
  respectively; both sites are owned by Signal Hill Petroleum (SHP). Collectively,
  both sites are zoned and entitled to accommodate up to 380 units of workforce
  housing which help the City meet its Regional Housing Needs Assessment
  (RHNA) allocation for the current Housing Element cycle.

  The City and the Housing Authority have accumulated funding for the
  development of affordable housing totaling approximately $10 million;
  notwithstanding this amount, an affordable housing developer would need to
  secure substantially more funding to design and construct both residential
  projects. The developer selected to work on the two sites will need to leverage
  the funding proposed as part of the NOFA and successfully receive funding from
  various sources including tax credits, grants, equity loans, and the Gateway
  Cities Affordable Housing Trust.

  Staff recommends issuing the NOFA to solicit proposals from qualified
  developers that will partner with the City and the property owner (SHP) to
  successfully build out the two sites. Given the complexities associated with
  financing affordable housing projects, the NOFA includes specific qualifications
  criteria and requires the proposers to provide a conceptual proforma analysis
  and a development plan for consideration as part of the evaluation process. A
  panel comprised of City staff and a representative from SHP will evaluate the
  proposals and recommend a developer to the City Council.
  Recommendation:

  Direct staff to issue the NOFA for the Orange Bluff and Walnut Bluff workforce
  housing sites and solicit proposals from affordable housing developers.
RECESS THE HOUSING AUTHORITY

(13)  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following Consent Calendar items are expected to be routine and
  non-controversial. Items will be acted upon by the Council at one time without
  discussion. Any item may be removed by a Council Member for discussion.
  a.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A LIST OF PROJECTS TO BE FUNDED BY
  SAFE, CLEAN WATER PROGRAM - MEASURE W FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2023-24

  Page 6 of 9
 City Council  Regular  April 25, 2023

  Summary:

  On November 6, 2018, Los Angeles County voters approved Measure W,
  commonly known as SCW. Measure W is funded by a parcel tax of 2.5 cents
  per square foot of impermeable area within the Los Angeles County Flood
  Control District (District). This parcel tax is expected to generate up to $285
  million per year countywide for SCW. SCW is intended to improve water quality
  in a manner that achieves additional benefits such as increasing water supply
  and investing in the health and well-being of Los Angeles County communities.
  The City Council will consider adopting a resolution to incorporate a list of
  projects and programs to be funded by the Safe, Clean Water Program (SCW) -
  Measure W for Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-24.
  Recommendation:

  Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, approving the List of projects AND PROGRAMS FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2023-24 to be funded BY safe, clean water program - Measure W
  FUNDS
  b.  RESOLUTION ADOPTING POLICIES AND PROCEDURES TO PRIORITIZE
  WATER SERVICE TO AFFORDABLE HOUSING PROJECTS PURSUANT TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65589.7

  Summary:

  The City has begun implementation of the required programs in the 6th Cycle
  Housing Element Update (HEU). Pursuant to Government Code 65589.7, the
  Signal Hill Water Department must prepare a policy for adoption by the City
  Council to prioritize water service to affordable housing projects.
  Recommendation:

  Adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING POLICIES AND PROCEDURES TO PRIORITIZE
  WATER AND SEWER SERVICES TO AFFORDABLE HOUSING PROJECTS
  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65589.7
  c.  FEE WAIVER REQUEST FOR THE SPRINGS OF HOPE GRIEF CARE
  CENTER (SPRINGS OF HOPE) PRIVATE MEMORIAL EVENT

  Summary:

  Staff received a request from Springs of Hope for a fee waiver in the amount of
  $1,760 (including staff costs and equipment) for the use of the Signal Hill Public
  Library Community Room and Zinnia Courtyard for a private event in

  Page 7 of 9
 City Council  Regular  April 25, 2023

  remembrance of Mr. Ron Settles, scheduled on Friday, June 2, 2023.
  Recommendation:

  Review and approve a waiver of fees for use of Signal Hill Public Library
  Community Room and Zinnia Courtyard, staff costs, and equipment.
  d.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS AND MONTHLY TRANSACTION REPORT

  Summary:

  The Schedule of Investments is a listing of all surplus funds invested for both the
  City and the Successor Agency to the former Signal Hill Redevelopment Agency
  as of the date shown on the report. The monthly transaction report provides the
  changes in investments for the prior month.
  Recommendation:

  Receive and file.
  e.  WARRANT REGISTER DATED APRIL 25, 2023

  Summary:

  The Warrant Register is a listing of all general disbursements issued since the
  prior warrant register and warrants to be released upon City Council approval.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize payment of the Warrant Register dated April 25, 2023.
  f.  APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES

  Summary:

  Regular Meeting of April 11, 2023.
  Recommendation:

  Approve the meeting minutes.
(14)  COUNCIL AGENDA--NEW BUSINESS

  COUNCIL MEMBER WILSON
  COUNCIL MEMBER JONES
  COUNCIL MEMBER COPELAND
  VICE MAYOR WOODS
  MAYOR HANSEN
(15)  ADJOURNMENT

  Tonight’s meeting will be adjourned to the next regular meeting of the Signal Hill City
  Council to be held on Tuesday, May 9, 2023, at 7:00 p.m. (hybrid meeting format,
  including in-person, and video and teleconference participation options). Instructions to
  Page 8 of 9
 City Council  Regular  April 25, 2023

  participate in the meeting will be provided on the meeting agenda.
CITIZEN PARTICIPATION

  Routine matters are handled most quickly and efficiently if contact is made with the City
  department directly concerned. However, if you would like to request that a matter be
  presented for City Council consideration, you may do so by writing to the City Council,
  City Clerk, or City Manager. The deadline for agenda items is 12 noon on the Tuesday
  preceding the Council and Agency meetings. The complete agenda, including back up
  materials is available on the City website on the Friday preceding the meeting.

  If you need special assistance beyond what is normally provided to participate in City
  meetings, the City will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner.
  Please call the City Clerk's office at (562) 989-7305 at least 48 hours prior to the
  meeting to inform us of your particular needs and to determine if accommodation is
  feasible.
